2. The appellants in this case are seeking suspension of their sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.
3. The appellants have been convicted vide judgment dated 09.10.2023 and sentenced vide order dated 12.10.2023 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge- 6th -cum- Special Judge POCSO Act, Banka in Special POCSO Case No. 19 of 2022 arising out of Chandan P.S. Case No. 58 of 2022 for the offences under Sections 364, 302, 376(DB), 201 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code (in short 'IPC') and under Section 4 of the POCSO Act.

4. As per the prosecution story, uncle of the deceased Uttam Kumar Poddar (informant) alleged that on the day of Holi Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1222 of 2023(6) dt.16-05-2024 i.e. on 19.03.2022 at around 2:00 PM his niece (deceased), about eight years old, went missing.
It is alleged that her body was recovered near the railway station at around 11:00 PM in a gruesome state.

It is alleged that she was raped and, thereafter, murdered by accused namely, Sagar Soni,
Doman Paswan, Ajay Barnwal and Shridhar Kumar.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the star witness in this case is the child (PW-4)
who was playing with his sister when she was taken away by the driver of the toto vehicle.
It is submitted that in course of trial, the said child witness has identified Sagar Soni as the person who had taken away the victim girl on his toto.
The said Sagar Soni is the owner of the vehicle.

6. Learned counsel further submits that it is stated about Doman Paswan (appellant of Cr. APP (DB)
No. 1211 of 2023) that he was the driver of the vehicle but there is no evidence at all on the record that at the time the victim girl was taken away by the toto vehicle, it was being driven by Doman Paswan.
There is no witness on the point that the victim girl was seen in the company of Doman Paswan.
7. It is further submitted that police has not seized any incriminating material from the possession of Doman Paswan.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1222 of 2023(6) dt.16-05-2024 8.

On behalf of the appellant Ajay Kumar Barnwal (appellant in Criminal Appeal (DB) No. 1222 of 2023), it is stated that there is no witness who has seen the victim girl in the company of this appellant.

In course of investigation, police had seized his banyan and undergarments which were washed and those were sent for chemical examination to the Forensic Science Laboratory (in short 'FSL') but the FSL report disclosed that no blood stain or semen could be found on the clothes of Ajay Kumar Barnwal.

It is further submitted that the appellant Sridhar Kumar @ Sridhar Barnwal @ Chhotu (appellant in Criminal Appeal (DB) No. 1134 of 2023) and Ajay Kumar Barnwal both have been implicated in this case only because it is stated that they had very good friendship with the two constables of R.P.F who were living in the R.P.F Barrack near Chandan Railway Junction.

9. Learned counsel submits that in course of investigation the help of Dog Squad was also taken and it was found that on the bed of the constables of the barrack namely, Vimal Kumar and Basudev,
some blood were lying.
In FSL examination, those blood have been found to be that of human body.
Learned counsel submits that at the relevant time when these appellants were chargesheeted, the investigation against Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1222 of 2023(6) dt.16-05-2024
Vimal Kumar and Basudev both the constables were kept pending and later on, police has submitted chargesheet against them and they are facing trial.
It is submitted that at this stage the appellants deserve suspension of sentence and release on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the informant as well as learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State jointly submit that it is a case based on circumstantial evidence.

The toto belong to Sagar Soni but in course of investigation, it has transpired in the statement of Sagar Soni that it was Ajay Kumar Barnwal who had asked him to come with toto vehicle and when he refused to do so then on his insistence at about 6:00 P.M. Doman Paswan had taken the vehicle.
It has come in evidence that Ajay Barnwal and Sridhar both were having very close friendship with the two constables of the R.P.F in whose bedroom the Sniffer Dogs had entered and stopped.
It is submitted that the learned trial court, having found that the circumstantial evidences are available to complete the chain, convicted the appellants.
11. We have heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for the informant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State and also perused the records.
We find Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1222 of 2023(6) dt.16-05-2024 that it is a case based on circumstantial evidence and last seen theory.

At this stage, this Court would not go into the thread- bare discussions into the evidences which are available on the records, suffice is to say that on reading the materials available on the record, this Court is not prima-facie convinced to grant privilege of suspension of sentence and release on bail to the appellants at this stage.

12. Since it is a case in which the appellants have been convicted under the provisions of IPC as well as the POCSO Act, we are of the opinion that the appeal be heard on an early date in terms of the statutory scheme of the POCSO Act.
13. Liberty is granted to the appellants to move an application for early hearing.

(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J) ( Shailendra Singh, J) maynaz/-lekhi/-
